project.name: Problem Field
project.question: How might one surface help us make sense of a problem across scattered source material without losing fidelity or jumping prematurely to solutions?

sources.title: Initial problem-space brief
sources.summary: A description of moving between calls, source material, chat, and flat visual boards while trying to understand the core problem.

cards.title: Caught between two surfaces
cards.body: The thinking is happening between a visual board and a chat, with neither surface holding the complete picture.

sourceRef.quote: I'm kind of floating in between the two, trying to take things from the chat and represent them on the board.

cards.title: Insights disappear in translation
cards.body: Moving material between tools is not neutral; context and insight are being dropped along the way.

sourceRef.quote: I'm finding that I'm losing things.

cards.title: Every handoff asks for reinterpretation
cards.body: Copying an insight from transcript to chat to board forces it to be re-summarized, relocated, and separated from its source.

cards.title: The board stores layout, not understanding
cards.body: Flat canvases can show where objects sit, but do not naturally preserve why they are related or what evidence supports them.

cards.title: The real tax is fragmented attention
cards.body: The problem is not merely scattered files. The sensemaking loop itself is split across tools, forcing the user to act as the integration layer.

cards.title: What must remain inspectable?
cards.body: Which links between source, excerpt, interpretation, and pattern must stay one click away for the result to remain trustworthy?

cards.title: What should an agent be allowed to change?
cards.body: Can the agent surface and arrange possible patterns without collapsing evidence into conclusions or taking ownership of judgment?
